children: Editor's note: This article was updated at 945a ET on Sept. 28 with confirmation that a formal rule for the standards has been issued.
The Trump administration on Monday issued a rule that lowers fuel economy standards compared to the trajectory they were on due to rules established during the Biden administration.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy unveiled the new rule as part of the "Freedom Means Affordable Cars" initiative. The secretary claims the initiative will cut the cost of the average new vehicle by $1300, reduce vehicle injuries and deaths through sales of safer new cars, and save Americans $138B over the next five years.
The rule also ends a Biden 2021 executive order that aimed to have half of all new vehicle sales in the US electric by 2030.

President Trump on Saturday hinted at the changes. "These new Standards will take the waste out of building cars in America," he wrote on Truth Social. "That means LOWER PRICES, saving families thousands on a new, beautiful, and safe car — Far better than the Environmental Monsters that we were building heretofore."
Trump added that under his administration, more than $100B is being invested in American automobile manufacturing.

The new rule is expected to reduce yearly oil consumption in 2050 by about 1.3 billion barrels compared to 2024, according to a US Transportation Department news release. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) estimates the new standards would achieve a fleet average fuel economy of 34.9 miles (ca. 56 kilometers) per gallon by model year 2031. In model year 2024, the figure was 30.1 miles (ca. 48 kilometers) per gallon.

In late August, Duffy said that the administration would soon unveil a "common-sense fuel economy standard because we want ​Detroit to build cars that Americans want to buy—not cars that Democrats want Washington ​to build."

In December 2025, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration proposed a fleetwide average of 34.5 miles (ca. 56 kilometers) per gallon by 2031. Biden had called for 50.4 miles (ca. 81 kilometers) per gallon.

While NHTSA projected its proposal would lead to savings of $930 per vehicle, it would add 100 billion gallons of fuel consumption through 2050, increase carbon dioxide emissions by 5%, and boost fuel spending by $185B, according to a Reuters report.

title: Trump issues rule lowering fuel economy standards, ends Biden EV mandate
